items.prompt: Why split boundary observation weight in the discrete ES calculation?

options.text: To reduce every reported risk number arbitrarily
options.why: The chosen tail definition determines the weight, not a desired answer.

options.text: To remove inconvenient losses from the dataset
options.why: The full empirical distribution is retained.

options.text: To use exactly the required 1-q tail mass
options.why: Including all or none of a tied boundary can use a different mass.

options.text: To claim half an independent real observation was collected
options.why: Fractional probability weight is not extra independent data.

items.explanation: The definition averages a fixed upper-tail probability share, with the boundary fraction needed to make that share exact.
